correctness.rationale: For odd \(C^3\) increasing drag on the compact invariant speed interval, the stationary transport currents satisfy \(J'=-rp\) and \(K'=-(r+2\lambda)q\), with \(J(0+)=r/2\). Eliminating the orientation difference yields \((\Sigma^2-g^2)p'=(g'-r-2\lambda)J+2g(g'-r-\lambda)p\). At equality \(r+2\lambda=g'(0)\), differentiation gives \(p''(0+)=2g'(0)\lambda p(0)/\Sigma^2>0\). The positive no-tumble-since-last-reset subpopulation has velocity density \(h_r(v)=r\exp[-(r+\lambda)T(v)]/[2(\Sigma-g(v))]\), where \(T(v)=\int_0^vdu/(\Sigma-g(u))\). Its terminal singularity forces full-density divergence under \(r+\lambda<g'(v_*)\); continuity then gives two intervening minima in the combined cusp regime. The zero-current reset-free formula yields the weak-reset local inversion. Five independent finite-volume consistency checks using the actual packaged `verify.py` passed; they corroborate but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 nonlinear inertial run-and-tumble study investigates stationary velocity-density morphology by numerical plots. The exact local line \(r+2\lambda=g'(0)\) and separately proven divergence condition \(r+\lambda<g'(v_*)\) give an explicit coexistence region with a central cusp, two divergent terminal peaks and intervening minima. For \(g'(0)/2<\lambda<g'(0)\), arbitrarily weak resetting turns a smooth reset-free minimum into a cusp maximum while terminal singularities can persist. These natural physical regime boundaries help interpret finite-resolution distributions. The result is not a complete mode count or a new master equation.
